paper_metadata.title: Understanding improved high temperature strength of Mo-Si-B alloy at 1100 – 1300 °C based on ZrB2 addition

evidence.quote: In this study the influence of ZrB2 addition on microstructure and high temperature compressive strength (1100 ◦C – 1300 ◦C) of Mo-12Si-8.5B (at. %) alloy was investigated.

The low angle grain boundaries (LAGB, interface orientation between 2◦ to 15◦), which are related to the dynamic recovery with series of dislocations after deformation, are more easily observed in α-Mo grains but not in Mo3Si and Mo5SiB2 phases since the hard Mo3Si and Mo5SiB2 phases are difficult to deform due to their high strength.
The addition of ZrB2 induces the generation of Zr-rich nanoparticles as see in TEM images (Fig. 2), which significantly impede the grain growth of the Mo-Si-B alloy.
For MSB-1.5, MSB-2.5 and MSB-1.5-H alloys, it is observed that the nearly spherical Zr-rich particles are mostly dispersed within grains and partly distributed at grain interfaces.

evidence.quote: The TEM result of the deformed MSB-1.5 sample after compressed at 1100 ◦C shows that dislocation pile-up observed at the gain boundary (Fig. 5 (d)), which result in the obvious grain boundary strengthening effect.

evidence.quote: It can be seen that dislocations pinning by the intragranular Zr-rich particles can be observed commonly in the TEM images, and moreover the dislocations near the intragranular particles usually exhibit very curved shapes showing strong interactions between them and the nanosized Zr-rich particles (Fig. 4 (b) and (c)), which is a reliable evidence of particle strengthening.
